messages:
Nora (AE): Quick sync: RetailBank wants a 30-day Dedicated POC in us-west-2. They require a single-address allowlist for outbound egress if possible, and ask if we can present the IP as a DNS name they can pin. Also they asked about cert rotation responsibilities for mTLS if we enable it. Need a procurement-ready line item for "30d Dedicated POC + mTLS ops". cc @Sam @Ivy

Sam (Solutions): We normally supply EIP(s) per Dedicated pool. Single EIP is doable but note HA risk. We can also provide a stable DNS name that resolves to current EIP(s) for convenience, but customers should still allowlist IPs since DNS can change on rotation. Pricing: will prepare a 30d reserved line item plus a one-time mTLS ops setup fee.

Ivy (Network): Network notes: outbound NAT from the pool is via allocated EIP(s). Options:
- Single /32 EIP: simplest for firewall teams.
- Two /32 EIPs: preferred for failover.
- DNS alias: we can publish a CNAME (e.g., rb-poc-egress.redwood.example) but we do not guarantee zero-change; if we rotate EIPs we update DNS TTLs. If they insist on a single static IP, warn about planned maintenance.

Tom (Infra): provisioning kicked off for small pool in us-west-2. Reserving 1 EIP per request; we can reserve extra if they want redundancy. ETA ~1.5 hours. We'll post the actual EIP(s) here.

Priya (Security): mTLS responsibilities: if enabled, customer provides CA bundle and client certs; we store the CA and enforce client cert validation on our edge. Rotation: customer must notify 7 days before rotation and provide new certs; ops will schedule a maintenance window. For formal procurement, include SOC2 and our mTLS handling note.

Sam (Solutions): Proposed POC steps for the customer:
1) Confirm desired pool size and whether they accept single EIP risk.
2) If mTLS: send CA bundle + cert validity/rotation plan.
3) We provision pool, reserve EIP(s), share IPs and DNS alias.
4) Customer allowlists IP(s) + tests via curl.

deploy-bot: action: requested small dedicated pool in us-west-2. ETA ~90m. EIP reservation in progress.

Ivy (Network): Firewall test once you have the key and IP(s):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_KEY" \
  --resolve dedicated-us-west-2.redwood.example:443:198.51.100.77 \
  "https://dedicated-us-west-2.redwood.example/v1/chat" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'
```
This forces the host to our EIP for validation.

Tom (Infra): Posted the IP: 198.51.100.77 (reserved). If they want redundancy we can add .78.

Nora (AE): Sending procurement the line item: "30-day Dedicated POC (small pool) - $X, one-time mTLS ops - $Y". Also sending SOC2 and Priya's mTLS note. Will update if they ask for single-IP SLA language.

Priya (Security): I'll attach the SOC2 PDF and a one-page mTLS operations note for their infosec reviewer.

Nora (AE): Customer replied: they accept single IP for POC but want a written note on what happens if we rotate IPs mid-POC. I'll draft that and loop back.
